purpose: Tire-compound index -> name. The save stores tire_compound as ordinal*1000+idx; idx (0..15) is a GLOBAL compound-catalog position. idx 0 = Stock is data-certain. The in-game Tire Compound MENU (video-captured 2026-08-23) gives the REAL FH6 compound NAMES, but the menu grid is NOT in save-index order and only shows a car's AVAILABLE compounds, so it does NOT by itself map name->index.
names_confidence: idx 0 = Stock is VERIFIED. All non-stock index->name assignments are UNVERIFIED best-effort — updated toward the real FH6 names from the menu video, but which index each name maps to is NOT proven (grid != index). Do not treat as authoritative until anchored (see below).

observed_fh6_menu_compounds.source: In-game Tire Compound menu, 2018 Exomotive Exocet Sport V8 XP-5 (ord 2866), video knE0jOvP9z.mp4 2026-08-23. Names are exact; grid POSITION is NOT the save index.
observed_fh6_menu_compounds.note: Stock tile literally reads 'Stock Tire Compound (Slick)' -> this car's stock tyre is a slick; the My Cars pane label 'Slick Tires' = STOCK (idx 0), not an upgrade.
not_seen_on_this_car: and whatever idx 11/12/15 are — the Exocet only offers its subset

index_map_status: STILL NEEDED. The menu gives names but not indices. To map name->index GLOBALLY (the index is global, so one car suffices): install + save a distinctive compound on ONE car, decode the saved tune, read tire_compound%1000 = that compound's index. A handful of installs (e.g. Drag, Snow, Offroad Race, Slick Race) on the Exocet anchors those indices for the whole garage. This also resolves 11/12/15.
